chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Cancelled within 24 hours unless you confirm your card"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Cancelled within 24 hours unless you confirm your card"
dang.description:
Open the app you booked with. If the reservation shows as confirmed, ignore the message and report it there. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "We could not find your booking in our new system"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "We could not find your booking in our new system"
dang.description:
Never reconfirm through a link. Your confirmation email or app already proves the booking. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Your hotel is overbooked, pay the difference here"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Your hotel is overbooked, pay the difference here"
dang.description:
Call the hotel on the number from its own website and ask whether your room is still there. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: Can a hotel cancel my booking by text message?

dang.title: Can a hotel cancel my booking by text message?
dang.description:
A real cancellation shows up in your booking, with the reason, in the app or site you used. A message that threatens cancellation unless you pay through a link is the scam itself. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: The message had my name and booking number. Doesn't that make it real?

dang.title: The message had my name and booking number. Doesn't that make it real?
dang.description:
No. Those details can come from a hotel account that was broken into. Judge the message by what it asks you to do, not by what it knows. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: My booking is non-refundable. Should I be more worried?

dang.title: My booking is non-refundable. Should I be more worried?
dang.description:
The terms are the same either way: they live in your booking. A non-refundable rate makes people panic faster, which is why scammers like it, but it doesn't change how you check. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: What if I ignore it and the cancellation was real?

dang.title: What if I ignore it and the cancellation was real?
dang.description:
Then it will be in your booking app or your email from the booking site, and you can sort it out there. Checking costs you a minute; paying a scammer can't be undone. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-cancellation-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Transfer the remaining balance to our NEW bank account"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Transfer the remaining balance to our NEW bank account"
dang.description:
Don't transfer anything. Look at your booking: if a balance is due, it will say how and where to pay. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Your stay is unpaid. Scan the QR code to pay"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Your stay is unpaid. Scan the QR code to pay"
dang.description:
Check your booking for a payment status before you scan anything. Pay at the front desk if something is genuinely owed. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Pay the deposit by Zelle to secure 70% off"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Pay the deposit by Zelle to secure 70% off"
dang.description:
If a deal is real, you can book it on a site with a normal checkout. Anything that needs Zelle, wire or crypto is a no. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Is it ever normal to pay a hotel by bank transfer?

dang.title: Is it ever normal to pay a hotel by bank transfer?
dang.description:
Some small properties do take transfers, but it's stated on the booking page before you book. A transfer request that arrives later by message, to a "new" account, is the scam. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Is this site legit? It's much cheaper than the hotel's own website.

dang.title: Is this site legit? It's much cheaper than the hotel's own website.
dang.description:
Sometimes sites get better rates. Check that you pay on the site's own checkout page and that the booking then shows in your account. If the "deal" ends with a transfer or Zelle, walk away. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Can I get my money back after a bank transfer?

dang.title: Can I get my money back after a bank transfer?
dang.description:
Sometimes, if you move fast: call your bank the same day and ask for a recall. The longer you wait, the less likely it is. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Why would the hotel need my payment again if I already paid?

dang.title: Why would the hotel need my payment again if I already paid?
dang.description:
It wouldn't. Double-check your booking status. Claims of "unpaid" stays are a common way to get people to pay twice. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-bank-transfer-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Your card was declined, re-enter it within 2 hours"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Your card was declined, re-enter it within 2 hours"
dang.description:
Don't tap the link. Open your booking and look for a payment message from the booking site itself. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Reply with the 6-digit code to receive your refund"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Reply with the 6-digit code to receive your refund"
dang.description:
Never read a one-time code to anyone, for any reason. Real refunds don't need one. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Send a photo of your passport and a selfie holding your card"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Send a photo of your passport and a selfie holding your card"
dang.description:
Keep your ID for the front desk. If a hotel needs details before arrival, its booking system asks for them, not a chat. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: My card really might have failed. How do I check?

dang.title: My card really might have failed. How do I check?
dang.description:
Open the booking in the app or site you used. A real payment problem shows there, with a way to fix it in the same place. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Why would a scammer want a code if I haven't given my password?

dang.title: Why would a scammer want a code if I haven't given my password?
dang.description:
Many accounts send a code to your phone when someone tries to sign in or reset the password. Giving the code lets them finish taking over. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Do hotels ever ask for ID before arrival?

dang.title: Do hotels ever ask for ID before arrival?
dang.description:
Some ask for details through their official booking system or online check-in. They don't ask for passport photos or card selfies over WhatsApp. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Is it safe to give my card to the hotel at check-in?

dang.title: Is it safe to give my card to the hotel at check-in?
dang.description:
Yes, in person at the desk, and many hotels place a hold for incidentals. The risk is the channel, not the card. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-card-details-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Our app chat is unavailable. Continue on WhatsApp"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Our app chat is unavailable. Continue on WhatsApp"
dang.description:
Reply only inside the booking app. If the app chat truly isn't working, use the help section in the app itself. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "We have no record of your booking from the app. Pay us directly"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "We have no record of your booking from the app. Pay us directly"
dang.description:
Contact the booking app right away; it's their job to sort it out. Call the hotel on its official number to check. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Book direct on our site and save 40%, bank transfer only"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Book direct on our site and save 40%, bank transfer only"
dang.description:
Find the hotel's website yourself through a search engine or map, never through a link in a message. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: A hotel I booked on a big booking site messaged me on WhatsApp. Is that normal?

dang.title: A hotel I booked on a big booking site messaged me on WhatsApp. Is that normal?
dang.description:
Friendly WhatsApp messages before arrival do happen. The warning sign is what comes next: a payment link, a card request, or a push to stop using the app. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: The hotel says it never got my booking. What should I do?

dang.title: The hotel says it never got my booking. What should I do?
dang.description:
Contact the booking app first; it has your payment and confirmation. Then call the hotel on the number from its official website. Don't pay again through a link. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: Is booking direct with the hotel cheaper?

dang.title: Is booking direct with the hotel cheaper?
dang.description:
Sometimes. If you want to book direct, go to the hotel's real website yourself and pay on its checkout. Never use a link from an unexpected message. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: How do I know a WhatsApp number really belongs to the hotel?

dang.title: How do I know a WhatsApp number really belongs to the hotel?
dang.description:
Compare it with the number on the hotel's own website or map listing. If it's different, treat the chat as untrusted. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-whatsapp-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "City tax must be paid online before arrival"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "City tax must be paid online before arrival"
dang.description:
Check your booking: it says whether city tax is included or paid at the property. Pay it there, not by link. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "We found damage after your checkout, pay to avoid legal action"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "We found damage after your checkout, pay to avoid legal action"
dang.description:
Don't pay. Ask the hotel, through the booking app or its official email, for the claim in writing. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Got this from your hotel? "Your total didn't include a service fee and a staff tip"

dang.title: Got this from your hotel? "Your total didn't include a service fee and a staff tip"
dang.description:
Compare with the total on your booking. If it matches, there's nothing more to pay before arrival. Three real examples and what to do if you already paid:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Is the hotel allowed to charge city tax on top of my booking?

dang.title: Is the hotel allowed to charge city tax on top of my booking?
dang.description:
Yes, in many cities. Your booking normally says if it's included or paid at the property. You pay it at the hotel, not through a link sent by message. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: A booking site added fees at checkout. Is that a scam?

dang.title: A booking site added fees at checkout. Is that a scam?
dang.description:
Not necessarily, but you should see every fee before you pay. A fee that shows up later, by text, with a deadline, is the warning sign. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Can a hotel charge me for damage after I leave?

dang.title: Can a hotel charge me for damage after I leave?
dang.description:
It can make a claim, usually through the booking site with details and evidence. You don't have to pay a link in a threatening message. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Do I have to tip because the message asked?

dang.title: Do I have to tip because the message asked?
dang.description:
No. Tips are your choice and handled in person. A text asking you to pay a tip online is not from the hotel. The full guide, with real messages:

https://ratesbyroom.com/hotel-fake-fee-scam/

chu_de: Ten hotel messages. Can you tell which ones are scams?

dang.title: Ten hotel messages. Can you tell which ones are scams?
dang.description:
Some are normal hotel texts, some are scams that took real money. Pick scam or real for each one and see the red flags you missed. Takes about a minute:

https://ratesbyroom.com/scam-quiz/

chu_de: Would you pay this hotel? Most people miss at least two of these

dang.title: Would you pay this hotel? Most people miss at least two of these
dang.description:
A short quiz built from real hotel messages, real and fake mixed together. You see why after every answer:

https://ratesbyroom.com/scam-quiz/

chu_de: Scam or real? A one-minute quiz with real hotel texts

dang.title: Scam or real? A one-minute quiz with real hotel texts
dang.description:
Deadlines, new bank details, "your card was declined". Try it before the next message lands in your inbox:

https://ratesbyroom.com/scam-quiz/

dang.title: Got a text from your hotel asking you to pay? Paste it here first
dang.description:
The free checker reads the message and points out the red flags: deadlines, new bank details, pay links, requests for codes. Nothing is saved:

https://ratesbyroom.com/check-message/

chu_de: Not sure a hotel message is real? Check it in 10 seconds

dang.title: Not sure a hotel message is real? Check it in 10 seconds
dang.description:
Paste the text, see which lines are red flags and what to do next. Free, no sign-up:

https://ratesbyroom.com/check-message/

chu_de: Before you pay a hotel through a link, run the message through this

dang.title: Before you pay a hotel through a link, run the message through this
dang.description:
Most hotel scams use the same few lines. The checker spots them and tells you how to confirm with the hotel directly:

https://ratesbyroom.com/check-message/
